newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices bounce back on stock shortage.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices bounce back on stock shortage.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Tuesday bounced back after recent losses on the local market, traders said.
Mill buying was slow on reports of renewed rain in producing centres but a shortage of ready stock lifted prices.
"Heavy and widespread rain in the producing centres has disrupted transportation of cotton from there to consuming centres," one broker said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi looked up by 10 rupees at 1,010/1,085 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 moved up by 5/20 rupees at 2,070/2,085 rupees per maund.

In the Gujarat segment, Kalyan cotton bounced back by 100 rupees at 14,200/14,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Kala-ginned was steady at 12,400/12,500 rupees per candy and wagad cotton at 13,200.
Overall sentiment was subdued at the close of the session amid sluggish enquiries from millers as well as due to rain in producing centres.
